destination.title: Electroweak scale origins and Higgs-sector constraints
destination.question: How can the electroweak scale be generated, stabilized or selected, and how do Higgs potentials, cosmology and consistency tests constrain proposed explanations?
destination.summary: The original region has numerical membership but no supplied verbal scientific scope to endorse. Its direct hierarchy questions form a useful core, surrounded by distinct questions about stability, inflation, dark energy, thermal transitions and observations. The proposed organization preserves those distinctions without excluding ordinary or pre-Swampland work.

sources.title: Ghost-Free Higher Derivative Quantum Gravity, the Hierarchy and the Cosmological Constant Problems

sources.title: Constraining the EW Hierarchy from the Weak Gravity Conjecture

sources.title: The Fundamental Need for a SM Higgs and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: The Higgs potential supplies a known positive-energy stationary configuration in the Higgs directions. The relevant energy is the electroweak barrier above the broken-phase minimum, rather than the observed dark-energy density.

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: Can motion of another modulus supply the missing gradient when the Higgs is moved from the broken phase to its symmetric point?

evidence.text: Can additional scalar directions keep the complete gradient large enough at the Higgs-symmetric point? Model 2 is examined with μ ≪ v and bounded φ, while its full interactions and kinetic metric occur on omitted pages.

sources.title: Do We Live in the Swampland?

evidence.text: The reference electroweak theory contains the Higgs radial mode and quintessence. The relevant test point is the symmetric configuration H = 0, where the Higgs potential is positive but its radial derivative vanishes.

sources.title: Do We Live in the Swampland?

evidence.text: Can an electroweak singlet remove positive stationary points while preserving a stable broken Higgs vacuum? The model couples S linearly to H squared and includes a quadratic singlet mass term.

sources.title: The Cosmological Constant and the Electroweak Scale

evidence.text: Can the statistical preference for an exponentially small positive cosmological constant in racetrack Kähler uplift compactification also generate a Higgs-like mass scale near the electroweak scale, after matching an ensemble percentile to the paper’s observed cosmological-constant benchmark?

sources.title: The Self-Tuning of the Cosmological Constant and the Holographic Relaxion

evidence.text: Can holographic brane worlds simultaneously admit self-tuning of the cosmological constant and electroweak symmetry breaking with a Higgs mass much smaller than the brane cutoff, for suitable potentials without finely tuned parameters?

evidence.text: Can cosmological survival near an ultralight scalar's potential maximum select a Higgs mass below heavier new physics, also permit anthropically small vacuum energy, and produce observable dark-energy evolution?

evidence.text: How can supersymmetry, string compactification and a possible multiverse address the electroweak and cosmological-constant naturalness problems, and what prevents accommodation of small parameters from becoming a predictive explanation?

evidence.text: Can an infinite spectrum with modular-invariance-induced cancellations stabilize the electroweak scale and address the cosmological constant without spacetime supersymmetry or an extra-dimensional hierarchy mechanism? evidence.text: Can a landscape finely scan vacuum energy and Higgs mass parameters while leaving dimensionless couplings nearly fixed, thereby retaining particle-physics predictivity and motivating sparse TeV-scale extensions through environmental selection?

evidence.text: Can a cancellation in Higgs self-interactions require new physics even when its mass is far below the Planck scale?

sources.title: QCD, Flavor, and the de Sitter Swampland

evidence.text: What remains outside the proposed hierarchy argument? The source identifies the large-positive-Higgs-mass phase and unknown nonperturbative QCD or Standard Model phenomena as unresolved domains.

sources.title: Ghost-Free Higher Derivative Quantum Gravity, the Hierarchy and the Cosmological Constant Problems

evidence.text: A derivative gauge-fixing term is added, and the momentum-space quadratic operator is decomposed into spin-two, spin-one and two spin-zero projectors. The author inverts that operator and takes α→0 to remove gauge-dependent projector terms.

sources.title: Constraining Neutrino Masses, the Cosmological Constant and BSM Physics from the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Substitute the assumed neutrino mass formula into the eigenmass cap while holding the Yukawa, vacuum energy and specified extra spectrum fixed.

sources.title: Constraining the EW Hierarchy from the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Specify the infrared spectrum, vary the compactification radii, and compare positive fermionic Casimir terms with negative photon and graviton terms. The source uses earlier potential calculations to decide whether the fermions intervene early enough and to bound their masses.

sources.title: Quantum gravity fluctuations flatten the Planck-scale Higgs potential

evidence.text: Compute beta functions using the Wetterich functional renormalization-group equation with a Litim-type regulator. Although the functional equation is exact, the calculation restricts the effective action to finitely many operators and employs a background-field linear metric split.

sources.title: A warped relaxion

evidence.text: Chiral rotations move anomalous couplings into fermion masses; confinement generates the cosines. The initial matching gives Λ_F⁴ = mχΛ_GF³, M_F = Λ_IR, Λ_f⁴ = m_NΛ_Gf³ and M_f² = m_Nm_L/(yỹ). The barrier relations are leading matching after integrating out L and Lᶜ, valid for m_N ≪ m_L and |yỹ|H² ≪ m_L² throughout the Higgs range considered. The condensing χ pair must lie below Λ_GF, and the light fermion eigenstate after doublet-singlet mixing must lie below Λ_Gf. One-loop potentials and higher-dimensional operators assess radiative stability.

sources.title: The Fundamental Need for a SM Higgs and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Count light fermionic minus bosonic degrees of freedom across confinement. Electroweak pseudo-Goldstone masses are estimated at one loop, with charged electromagnetic contributions m² ≃ (α_em/4π)Λ_QCD² and W/Z contributions assumed comparable in size.

sources.title: Higgs physics as a window beyond the MSSM (BMSSM)

evidence.text: Can a broken additional gauge interaction provide Higgs quartic corrections while its vector multiplet is integrated out?

sources.title: Sliding naturalness: cosmological selection of the weak scale

evidence.text: Can post-reheating cosmological dynamics select a small, nonzero weak scale despite a high Higgs-sector cutoff, independently of the inflationary sector and optionally independently of a solution to strong CP?

sources.title: Theory Closing Talk

evidence.text: What explains the electroweak scale after the LHC's then-null direct searches, and which assumptions underlying Higgs naturalness could be relaxed to motivate alternatives to symmetry-based explanations?

sources.title: Novel bounds from the weak gravity and Festina-Lente conjectures

evidence.text: What conditional bounds follow from combining electric and magnetic WGC/Festina-Lente conjectures with fifth-force models, Higgs vacuum assumptions, inflationary reheating and scalar naturalness?

sources.title: Higgs mass implications on the stability of the electroweak vacuum

evidence.text: Under the December 2011 Higgs-mass hypothesis 124–126 GeV, what are the Standard Model vacuum stability and metastability bounds, and what do they imply for reheating, thermal leptogenesis, and heavy right-handed neutrinos?

sources.title: Exciting Implications of LHC Higgs Boson Data

evidence.text: Do the apparently Standard-Model-like Higgs observations available in 2018 provide clues favoring a supersymmetric two-doublet decoupling theory, TeV-scale superpartners, and a compactified string/M-theory ultraviolet completion?

sources.title: Constraining power of asymptotic safety for scalar fields

evidence.text: Does asymptotically safe gravity, through a predicted non-minimal Higgs coupling, stabilize or destabilize a potentially metastable Higgs vacuum in the high-curvature early universe?

sources.title: TF08 Snowmass Report: BSM Model Building

evidence.text: Which BSM mechanisms can address electroweak naturalness, strong CP, dark matter, baryogenesis, and flavor, and which theoretical and experimental developments guide their exploration? This is a Snowmass overview of contributed work rather than a single-model investigation.

sources.title: Higgs physics as a window beyond the MSSM (BMSSM)

evidence.text: Can discrepancies between measured Higgs masses and MSSM predictions, after determining the stop sector, reveal heavy additional degrees of freedom? Correlated Higgs and electroweakino observables provide further tests of the proposed effective interactions.

sources.title: Standard Model from A Supergravity Model with a Naturally Small Cosmological Constant

evidence.text: Can a string-motivated supergravity model automatically cancel electroweak Higgs vacuum energy against brane tension, preserve the racetrack mechanism for a statistically small positive cosmological constant, and yield the Standard Model particle sector?

sources.title: Naturalness: past, present, and future

evidence.text: How useful is naturalness as a pragmatic discovery strategy, and which historical and recent approaches address the strong CP, cosmological constant, and electroweak hierarchy problems under the experimental pressures described in this 2022 review?

sources.title: In Pursuit of New Paradigms: TASI 2024

evidence.text: Why is the Higgs apparently much lighter than the SM's UV completion? The lectures explore symmetry protection, dynamically selected tuning, and possible failures or restrictions of Wilsonian EFT reasoning.

sources.title: Higgs scalar potential in asymptotically safe quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can gravitational fluctuations near an asymptotically safe UV fixed point make the Higgs quartic coupling and mass term irrelevant, thereby predicting Higgs properties or explaining the electroweak–Planck hierarchy?

sources.title: Large hierarchies from attractor vacua

evidence.text: Can symmetry-controlled accumulation of vacua select a hierarchically small Higgs scale without low-energy physics regulating quadratic divergences, and can realistic implementations yield testable restrictions?

sources.title: The swampland conjecture and the Higgs expectation value

evidence.text: The setting combines the observed small dark-energy density with the electroweak Higgs potential. Vacuum-energy cancellation at the broken minimum leaves a much larger positive energy at the electroweak-symmetric point.

sources.title: Higgs physics as a window beyond the MSSM (BMSSM)

evidence.text: Which heavy-threshold interactions dominate Higgs observables when the new sector is approximately supersymmetric? The answer depends jointly on the heavy-scale ratios and η = cot β.

sources.title: Conference Summary and Outlook: Particle Physics Past, Present, and Future

evidence.text: What do the Standard Model's historical development and selected ICHEP2018 results imply for outstanding particle-physics questions, future experimental opportunities, and the guiding assumptions of naturalness, minimality and uniqueness?

sources.title: Stringy Completions of the Standard Model from the Bottom Up

evidence.text: Can the Higgs quartic and electroweak gauge couplings fit a positive-residue closed-string dressing at the high scale required by gauge-boson scattering?

sources.title: Horizontal gauge symmetry and masses of neutrinos

evidence.text: Can separate scalar sectors suppress horizontal gauge exchange while retaining electroweak symmetry down to a lower scale and ultimately preserving electromagnetism?

sources.title: New Approaches to the Hierarchy Problem and their Signatures from Microscopic to Cosmic Scales

evidence.text: How can microscopic physics generate an electroweak scale v with v/Λ ≪ 1? The dissertation explores neutral naturalness through cosmology and collider signatures, and noncommutative UV/IR mixing as an exploratory alternative.

sources.title: Evidence of the Big Fix

evidence.text: Does the proposed Big Fix maximum-entropy principle receive model evidence from late-universe radiation being maximized near the observed Higgs expectation value, when current quark masses, gauge couplings and the Higgs self-coupling are held fixed?

sources.title: A Note on the WGC, Effective Field Theory and Clockwork within String Theory

evidence.text: Can Higgsing produce effective theories that violate familiar strong/electric and magnetic WGC expectations while admitting string completion, and what restrictions does a heterotic completion impose on large Higgs charges and Abelian clockwork hierarchies?

sources.title: The Weak Scale from Weak Gravity

evidence.text: Can the electric weak gravity conjecture bound the electroweak scale parametrically below the Higgs-sector cutoff, while accommodating the magnetic WGC without trivializing that bound?

sources.title: The Lee-Wick standard model

evidence.text: The hierarchy problem asks why the Higgs mass remains small compared with a very high ultraviolet scale. This paper investigates whether higher derivative kinetic operators and their massive Lee-Wick resonances can remove quadratic radiative sensitivity while retaining a usable perturbative theory.

sources.title: Cosmological Relaxation of the Electroweak Scale

evidence.text: Can early-universe dynamics select an electroweak scale parametrically below the Higgs-sector cutoff, using technically natural small parameters without requiring new particles to cancel Higgs loops at the weak scale or an anthropic selection argument?

sources.title: Compactified 2HDM under the Non-SUSY AdS instability conjecture

evidence.text: Can a circle-compactified 2HDM accommodate the observed 125 GeV Higgs with radion stabilization and nonnegative vacuum energy, and what conditional heavy-Higgs restrictions follow from applying the non-SUSY AdS instability conjecture?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Can Higgsing preserve a weak existential WGC while violating stronger low-energy mass and cutoff requirements? A large integer Higgs charge produces a parametrically small residual coupling without automatically lowering all particle masses.

sources.title: The Hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter

evidence.text: Can the weak scale be the only fundamental short-distance scale, with the apparent Planck hierarchy arising from large compact spatial dimensions and Standard Model localization, while remaining compatible with laboratory and astrophysical constraints?

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: Can a quintessence gradient grow with the electroweak potential away from the observed Higgs vacuum while avoiding direct couplings to other visible matter?

sources.title: Higgs potential near-criticality from a de Sitter swampland-like condition

evidence.text: Must the Higgs potential itself be metastable? The paper's conclusion requires the branch in which no additional scalar supplies the deeper direction.

sources.title: Higgs mass and vacuum stability in the Standard Model at NNLO

evidence.text: What Higgs mass ensures absolute Standard Model vacuum stability up to the Planck scale after NNLO matching and running, and what do the resulting near-critical couplings imply for proposed Planck-scale boundary conditions and Higgs inflation?

sources.title: Higgs potential near-criticality from a de Sitter swampland-like condition

evidence.text: Could a restriction on the exact quantum effective potential explain the favored proximity of the Higgs potential to metastability? The paper presents this as an open explanatory possibility.

sources.title: Gauge hierarchy and metastability from Higgs-driven crunching

evidence.text: Can Higgs-driven cosmological crunching dynamically select a hierarchically small Higgs mass and a metastable electroweak vacuum, and what new physics would make the selected scale phenomenologically relevant?

sources.title: Paper-boat relaxion

evidence.text: Can a Higgs–axion potential instability preferentially select a small electroweak scale while allowing sub-Planckian scanning, an acceptable inflationary duration, and a QCD relaxion compatible with strong-CP relaxation and all cold dark matter?

sources.title: The String landscape, black holes and gravity as the weakest force

evidence.text: Could observing a weak gauge force constrain the energy scale of ultraviolet physics?

sources.title: Fine-tuned vs. natural supersymmetry: what does the string landscape predict?

evidence.text: Under an environmental restriction on the weak scale, are natural or electroweak-fine-tuned particle-physics scenarios more likely to emerge from the string landscape, and can their relative likelihoods be estimated?

sources.title: Is Gravity the Weakest Force?

evidence.text: Can a scalar force consistently be required to exceed gravity in our Universe, given tests of additional long-range forces? The answer depends on which particles must obey the inequality and whether the comparison concerns horizon distances or mixed ultraviolet and infrared physics.

sources.title: Attracting the electroweak scale to a tachyonic trap

evidence.text: Can rapid Higgs production near a symmetry-breaking point dynamically select the electroweak scale during inflation, using a fast-moving axion-like field and subsequent periodic trapping?

sources.title: Phenomenological aspects from vacuum stability and metastability in models with soft breaking of a \texorpdfstring{$U\left( 1\right)$}{lg} global symmetry

evidence.text: How do competing neutral electroweak minima constrain a softly broken U(1) two-Higgs-doublet model, its one-loop running, alignment benchmarks and scalar masses compatible with diphoton and electroweak precision fits?

sources.title: Simplest little Higgs model revisited: Hidden mass relation, unitarity, and naturalness

evidence.text: Which quantitative electroweak symmetry breaking predictions and fine-tuning constraints survive in the Simplest Little Higgs model when its scalar potential is renormalized as a continuum EFT, without assuming vanishing UV contributions?

sources.title: Protecting the stability of the electroweak vacuum from Planck-scale gravitational effects

evidence.text: Can symmetry suppress negative Planck-suppressed Higgs operators sufficiently to preserve EW-vacuum longevity, including gravitational backreaction and supersymmetry breaking above the SM instability scale?

sources.title: Horizontal gauge symmetry and masses of neutrinos

evidence.text: Could the scalars responsible for horizontal and electroweak breaking arise from fermion bound states rather than require a separate unexplained scalar sector?

sources.title: The collider landscape: which collider for establishing the SM instability?

evidence.text: Assuming no accessible new physics, which precision measurements and minimal collider specifications could establish SM vacuum instability and determine its scale, potentially providing structural information about a landscape of vacua?

sources.title: The String landscape, black holes and gravity as the weakest force

evidence.text: Can a very small gauge coupling coexist with a cutoff near the Planck scale?

sources.title: The Lee-Wick standard model

evidence.text: The proposed extension seeks Higgs-mass stabilization by adding higher derivative kinetic operators throughout the Standard Model. Each operator introduces a massive resonance rather than a new stable asymptotic particle, with its mass initially independent of the masses in other representations.

sources.title: Higgs physics as a window beyond the MSSM (BMSSM)

evidence.text: What is the constrained scalar-Higgs baseline against which new interactions are compared? Once v is fixed, the tree-level MSSM spectrum depends on mA and tan β.

sources.title: Is Gravity the Weakest Force?

evidence.text: Would adding a horizon-light scalar to ordinary particle physics force an observable fifth force? The example uses one canonical scalar and treats charged Standard Model particles as gauge-WGC states, making the universal scalar inequality applicable to ordinary matter.

sources.title: Electroweak relaxation of cosmological hierarchy

evidence.text: Can the approximate relation v_EW² ∼ Λ_DE Λ_inf connect electroweak symmetry breaking to the observed cosmic acceleration? The proposed reduction of the cosmological hierarchy problem remains conditional on explaining why the electroweak scale is small.

sources.title: Randall-Sundrum and Strings

evidence.text: Can phenomenologically viable string completions of Randall–Sundrum electroweak compositeness place string resonances parametrically above KK resonances, once Standard Model perturbativity and confinement-transition cosmology constrain the strong sector?

sources.title: Landscape Higgs boson and sparticle mass predictions from a logarithmic soft term distribution

evidence.text: How do landscape Higgs and sparticle mass distributions change when a logarithmic soft-term weight replaces the previously studied power-law weight, subject to anthropic electroweak selection?

sources.title: Weak Scale From the Maximum Entropy Principle

evidence.text: Can maximizing the final radiation of a postulated closed universe select a weak scale near the observed scale when the Higgs expectation value varies while dimensionless Standard Model couplings remain fixed?

sources.title: SUSY without the Little Hierarchy

evidence.text: Can a supersymmetric pseudo-Goldstone Higgs receive a sufficiently large quartic interaction without a corresponding large quadratic term, reducing the little-hierarchy tuning while allowing light stops and satisfying the paper's precision and perturbativity requirements?

sources.title: Monodromy Dark Matter

evidence.text: Represent fluctuations by a Gaussian ensemble with spectrum P(k), and estimate position-space variance growth through momentum integration. The authors numerically find the variance difference finite even where the initial variance diverges; its late-time growth is dominated by the largest exponent.

sources.title: Impact of First-order Electroweak Phase Transition on QCD Axion

evidence.text: The homogeneous axion equation θ̈+3Hθ̇+ma²(T)sinθ=0 is solved numerically across the three thermal phases, passing θ and θ̇ between phases. The kinetic and potential energy at TQCD is then redshifted to estimate the present relic density.

sources.title: Monodromy Dark Matter

evidence.text: Numerically evolve the homogeneous field, then insert that background into linear Fourier-mode equations and extract momentum-dependent exponential growth rates. The numerical examples take vanishing initial background velocity.

sources.title: Monodromy Dark Matter

evidence.text: Use Floquet theory and Hill's determinant as a second method for growth exponents. Approximate the infinite determinant by progressively larger central finite matrices; the authors report agreement with direct mode evolution.

sources.title: Impact of First-order Electroweak Phase Transition on QCD Axion

evidence.text: The gravitational-wave estimate uses sound-wave and MHD-turbulence templates, including finite sound-wave lifetime suppression. Transition strength and inverse duration are extracted from the effective potential and the temperature derivative of S3/T.

sources.title: Impact of First-order Electroweak Phase Transition on QCD Axion

evidence.text: The electroweak effective potential keeps tree-level scalar interactions and leading high-temperature T² thermal masses. FindBounce computes the O(3)-symmetric three-dimensional Euclidean bounce action; nucleation is estimated using Γd≈H⁴, implemented as S3(Tn)/Tn≈140.

sources.title: Euclidean wormholes, baby universes, and their impact on particle physics and cosmology

evidence.text: Can an ultralight axion provide the observed dark matter while its long Compton wavelength suppresses small structures? Misalignment abundance ties the mass m to the decay constant f and the initial displacement θ_i.

sources.title: The 3.5 keV Line from Stringy Axions

evidence.text: Hierarchical scalar-potential analysis: supersymmetric D/F-term stabilisation at O(V^-2), α′, string-loop, single-instanton and matter contributions at O(V^-3), followed by poly-instanton stabilisation of cp at O(V^(-3-p)), p>0.

sources.title: Axion Mass from Magnetic Monopole Loops

evidence.text: Interpret each winding contribution through a proper-time saddle and a relativistic worldline action including σ. Assess higher-derivative corrections using a perturbed dyon spectrum and a further saddle-point expansion.

sources.title: Wormhole-induced ALP dark matter

evidence.text: Abundance contours are combined with the cited Planck isocurvature bound βiso < 0.038 and then mapped from (ma, fa) to (ξ, fa) using the wormhole mass relation. Generic inflation treats the U(1) scalar as a spectator.

sources.title: The 3.5 keV Line from Stringy Axions

evidence.text: Order-by-order canonical normalisation in the inverse-volume expansion, followed by mass-matrix eigenvalue estimates and extraction of axion interaction scales. These are calculations reported by the authors, not reproduced here.

sources.title: Axion Mass from Magnetic Monopole Loops

evidence.text: Compute the one-loop vacuum energy either by summing Coleman-Weinberg-type contributions from dyon states or by a first-quantized Euclidean worldline path integral. Poisson resummation converts the dyon sum into a periodic winding expansion.

sources.title: Wormhole-induced ALP dark matter

evidence.text: Misalignment abundance is calculated separately for oscillation during radiation domination, reheating, or immediately after a thermal phase transition. During radiation domination, entropy conservation gives Ωa h² ≃ 0.12⟨θi²⟩(fa/(7×10^16 GeV))² sqrt(ma/(10^-21 eV)), using g* = g*,s = 106.75.
